what_happened: Job 20261027-202603-9dpf ("Refuse to queue stale approved proposals; ask for fresh approval", code) failed in planning, before any code was written. The critic said the reading misread the request. The request says to refuse when "an earlier job from the same source was closed as done". The reading and plan narrowed that to "a job cited in the proposal's source or evidence". Audience proposals set both source and evidence to the rating path and never cite a job, so rule (a) cannot fire for the incident class the request names, an approved audience proposal from an old rating. Records already link jobs to sources (Approved{job} to work_item to source), so the request's wording could have been implemented directly. The critic found one major finding and two minor findings. The minor ones: closing a blocked job writes "closed while blocked: {why}", so the plan's strip of "closed: " misses it. The Done rule also matches on reason text and ignores OutcomeState. There was one nit: a refused stale proposal stays open and is noted again on every drain run. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Planning checks that named functions exist and that demonstrations use real entry points. It does not make the reading or plan run the new rule's condition against the real shapes of the inputs it must catch, here the proposals audience.rs actually produces. It also does not check the request's own wording against the narrowed term. The reading replaced "same source" with "cited in source or evidence" without checking that the incident's proposals contain such citations. The plan's tests used the request's test wording ("cited job closed as done"), so they passed while the real case stayed uncovered. Planning has fixed rounds, keeps no partial plan and has no repair step, so a major finding that appears in round 1 and survives to round 5 loses all planning spend. The reading was accepted without a check that it kept the request's join (job to source via records). Reasons are also matched by text prefix instead of by recorded state.
prevention: Before a reading is accepted for a new refusal or matching rule, require it to name the incident's real input (here an audience proposal built by audience.rs) and show the rule's condition firing on it, using the request's own join wording (job to source through records) and not a narrowed reading. The plan must carry that case as a demonstration, and the plan must match on recorded outcome state, not on reason-text prefixes. The critic's round-1 misread finding should send the plan back to the reading, not to another plan round.
proposed_request: Refuse to queue an approved proposal when it is stale, and ask for fresh approval. A proposal is stale when an earlier job from the same source was closed as done. Find the source and the earlier job through the records: WorkDecision Approved{job} to work_item to source. Do not rely on a job being cited in the proposal's own source or evidence field, because audience proposals (audience.rs work_item) cite only the rating path. Put the check in approve_work after find_open and before approve_request and self.ask, so main.rs, approve_in_limit and drain approve_all all pass through it. Decide that a job closed as done by its recorded outcome state, not by reason text, and include a job closed while blocked ("closed while blocked: ..." in manage.rs). Acceptance: (1) an approved audience proposal from an old rating, whose source already has a job closed as done, is refused with a message asking for fresh approval; (2) a proposal whose cited job was closed as done is also refused; (3) a proposal with no earlier done job for its source is approved as before; (4) a landed or failed job whose reason merely begins with "Done" does not count; (5) a refused proposal does not produce a note on every later drain run. Show each case with a test that drives the real entry points on a seeded git repo.
